chunks: Muhammad ibn 'Ali ibn Mahbub, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Isma'il al-Hashimi, from 'Abd Allah ibn al-Hasan, from his grandfather 'Ali ibn Ja'far, from his brother Musa ibn Ja'far عليهما السلام, who said:
I asked him about a man who finds water in a watercourse or a pool, and fears that beasts may have drunk from it.

Should he perform ghusl (ritual bath) from it for janabah and make wudu (ablution) from it for salat (prayer), if he finds no other than it, while the water does not amount to a sa' for janabah nor a mudd for wudu, and it is scattered? What should he do?

He said: If his palm is clean, then let him take a handful of water with one hand and sprinkle it behind him, in front of him, to his right, and to his left. Then if he fears that it will not suffice him, he should wash his head three times, then wipe his skin with his hand; for that will suffice him, if Allah, the Exalted, wills.

key_terms.السَّاقِيَةِ: a watercourse or channel where water is found
key_terms.الْجَنَابَةِ: the state of major ritual impurity requiring ghusl
key_terms.صَاعًا: a measured quantity of water mentioned here for ghusl
key_terms.مُدًّا: a measured quantity of water mentioned here for wudu
key_terms.مُسْتَنْقَعًا: a stagnant pool or collected standing water

ai.seo_question: What should a person in janabah do if only a small amount of possibly animal-touched water is available?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling for one in a state of janabah who finds only a very small amount of water and fears contamination from beasts drinking from it. It outlines how to use limited water for purification in a minimal but sufficient way for ghusl and wudu when no alternative is available.
